terms.explanation: Introductory content for a page or section, often holding the logo and navigation.
Semantic element that wraps a block of navigation links.
The dominant, unique content of the page. Only one per page.
A thematic grouping of content, usually with its own heading.
Self-contained content that makes sense on its own, like a blog post or card.
Content indirectly related to the main content, such as a sidebar.
Closing content for a page or section: copyright, contact, links.
A group of input controls that submit data, e.g. a newsletter signup.
The top-level heading. Describes the main topic of the page.
One-dimensional layout model that aligns items in a row or a column.
Two-dimensional layout model with rows and columns.
Space between an element's content and its border.
Space outside an element's border, separating it from neighbours.
Applies styles only when conditions match, e.g. screen width (responsive design).
Element scrolls normally until it hits an offset, then sticks (e.g. a sticky header).
Adds a shadow around an element to create depth.
Rounds the corners of an element.
Pseudo-class that styles an element while the pointer is over it.
The large, eye-catching area at the top of a landing page with the main message.
A button or link that prompts the user to take a specific action.
Content visible without scrolling.
Empty space around elements that improves readability and focus.
Arranging elements by size, color and position to show their importance.
Testimonials, reviews or logos that build trust.
A three-line icon that opens a hidden navigation menu.
A contained box grouping related information, often with image, title and action.
Secondary navigation showing the user's location in the site hierarchy.
